output:
**TO WHOEVER KEEPS DUMPING RUBBISH IN MY BIN**

I live at No. 14, Aughrim Terrace. It’s a rented house, and mine is the grey Greenmount Bins wheelie bin with **14 painted on the lid in white**. It goes out on Tuesday night for collection on Wednesday morning.

For the past month or so, someone has been putting full bags of their rubbish into it every week. This isn’t the odd bottle or a bit of extra waste when the lid’s still up. It’s full black bags that aren’t mine.

I got home around 3am last Tuesday after working at a gig and found the bin so full that the lid wouldn’t close. There were three black bags in it that I didn’t put there, one of them containing nappies. There was also a gas bill envelope in one bag. The name had been torn off, but Aughrim Terrace was still visible. A neighbour across the road saw a car pull up on Tuesday evening, though they didn’t see who was in it.

Here’s the part you might not have bothered thinking about: Greenmount Bins charge by weight, at **€0.41 per kilo**. My bill is usually around **€25 for two months**. The last one was **€63.20**. So this isn’t harmless, and it isn’t just a favour between neighbours. I am literally paying to get rid of your crap.

I’m sick of it. I work nights, keep odd hours and generally get on with my own business, but don’t mistake that for being a pushover. I’m not funding somebody else’s rubbish because they can’t be arsed organising their own bin.

If you’re genuinely stuck, come and ask me. I’ll tell you who to ring. It’s not hard. Sneaking over under cover of darkness and stuffing nappies and torn-up post into somebody else’s bin is a miserable thing to do.

I’m not looking for an apology, an excuse or a big neighbourly drama. Whoever is doing it just needs to **stop**. Simple as that.

If it continues, I’ll be locking the bin with a padlock and taking whatever other steps are needed. Until then, keep your rubbish out of No. 14’s bin.

**The resident at No. 14**
